`ssl.SSLObject` does not support `suppress_ragged_eofs`.

Unlike `SSLSocket`:

- `suppress_ragged_eofs=True` causes unexpected EOF to appear as a normal EOF (`b""`).
- `suppress_ragged_eofs=False` causes an `ssl.SSLEOFError`.

For `SSLObject`, all EOF conditions that violate the TLS protocol are reported by raising `ssl.SSLEOFError`; there is no suppression option.
